holdings.thesis: HOLD: shares jumped +7.9% on 10/1 on renewed AI optical-connectivity/active-electrical-cable demand optimism; 14-analyst consensus remains Buy, avg PT $269.86 (10/4). COO Yat Tung Lam sold 50,000 shares in early Oct -- routine 10b5-1, continuation of the known chronic insider-selling pattern, not new. Return -21.3% vs. cost basis. Position ~6.7%.

HOLD: analyst views diverging -- JPMorgan reiterated Hold/$135 PT (10/2) vs. DA Davidson's Buy/$175 (9/29), consensus now Hold avg PT ~$124. Earnings-growth flag (-27.5% YoY) remains the known deliberate Max-tier sunset/AI-reinvestment story; next earnings now tracked 11/4/26 (corrected from 11/11). No new fundamental deterioration. Return +15.4% vs. cost basis. Position ~11.0%.

HOLD: CEO handover completed on schedule 9/30 (Singhal now CEO, Abuhoff Executive Chairman); same-day announcement of a new 'physical AI' lab producing motion data for humanoid/industrial robots, plus a beat on recent quarterly results (adj. EPS $0.41 vs. $0.21 est., revenue +57.8% YoY). Sector tailwind from Accenture's strong Q4 guidance. No red flags. Return -15.6% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.7%.

HOLD: new bullish coverage -- BMO Capital initiated Outperform/$329 PT and Vertical Research issued a Buy (9/30), adding to Wells Fargo's existing Overweight/$340 PT; stock down ~15% from its 9/8 high but bounced +2.46% on 10/2. No update on the Massachusetts permitting overhang or the Hagens Berman pre-litigation inquiry (both still dormant, no escalation). Next earnings 10/28/26. Return -21.6% vs. cost basis. Position ~8.3%.

HOLD: Gemini 4 'Argon' launch underwhelmed the Street (staged enterprise access vs. a hoped-for consumer-agent breakout); offsetting positives -- a multi-billion-$ TPU deal with Anthropic (up to 1M custom TPUs) and wins in two US antitrust suits. First-ever negative free-cash-flow quarter reported (~10/2-10/4) is a fresh watch item, not a sell trigger. Next earnings 10/27. Position ~15.0%, within the trim-tolerance band -- no action needed.

HOLD: on 10/2 Amazon confirmed it's exploring selling/leasing back ~$8B of Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs via an SPV and said it will raise AI-chip rental prices -- capital-structure optimization, not a demand problem. Analyst base remains Strong-Buy-heavy (57/59 buy-rated); AWS growth rate (last print 36.7%) is the key watch item into October earnings. Return -3.5% vs. cost basis. Position ~11.8%.

HOLD: Wells Fargo's 10/1 Equal-Weight downgrade is already known/priced; new crude-supply MOU with PetroVietnam (9/30) and a $9.4B quarterly capital-return/buyback announcement are incremental positives. Exxon asked SCOTUS to dismiss Boulder's climate-liability suit (oral argument 10/5) -- a watch item, not urgent. Next earnings 10/23. Return +2.5% vs. cost basis. Position ~11.0%.

HOLD: Crate & Barrel BNPL partnership confirmed (9/29) and a UK Amazon installment expansion (9/23); stock +5.5% over the week into 10/5. Coverage flags 'mixed near-term estimate trends' and credit-risk/leverage questions as background watch items -- no downgrade or guidance cut found. Next earnings 11/5. Return +6.9% vs. cost basis. Position ~6.0%.

HOLD: continued wave of bullish analyst action -- FBN Securities initiated Outperform/$325 PT, Wedbush assumed coverage Outperform/$275; guidance points to ~30% FY26 revenue growth; rating mix 90% Buy/6% Hold/4% Sell. Purely confirmatory, no negative catalyst. Return +23.5% vs. cost basis. Position ~4.8%.

HOLD: FDA approved an expanded Jaypirca indication (CLL/SLL); Phase 2 data show the weight-loss combo 'EloraTZP' beat tirzepatide alone, advancing to Phase 3 in Q4; Gate Bioscience licensing deal expanded to ~$870M (~10/4). Stock down ~6.7% over the past month ahead of 10/29 earnings (EPS est. $9.56, +36% YoY) -- pullback reads as sentiment/valuation-driven, not thesis-breaking. Return -1.5% vs. cost basis. Position ~3.8%.

HOLD: stock down ~43% YTD (rate-hike-fear-driven) despite record Q2 results (revenue $1.2B, members +35% to 15.8M, personal-loan originations +53% YoY to $10.7B); new SoFi Bank/Mastercard deal moves its entire $25B card program to stablecoin settlement. Decline reads as macro sentiment, not a fundamentals break. Next earnings 10/27. Return -6.6% vs. cost basis. Position ~2.7%.

HOLD: Truist reiterated Buy but trimmed its PT to $1,100 from $1,225 (10/5) -- a routine valuation reset, not a downgrade; separately CAT agreed to acquire dealer John Fabick Tractor Co. (9/29) and announced a $1.0B compact-equipment expansion in NC (9/30). Broad consensus still Buy (26 analysts, avg PT ~$976); Q2 beat stands (rev +24% YoY, adj. EPS $8.17 vs. $6.19 est., backlog $72B). Return +8.9% vs. cost basis. Position ~3.2%.

HOLD: new analyst support -- Bank of America initiated coverage with a Buy/$60 PT, and Mizuho reiterated Buy citing the approaching Superion 256 ramp (~19% implied upside). Consensus 10 Buy/4 Hold/1 Sell, avg PT ~$63.83. No negative catalysts found; SkyWater acquisition integration and raised FY26 guidance ($280-290M) remain the core thesis. Return +14.1% vs. cost basis. Position ~2.5%.

HOLD: stock jumped ~6.2% on 10/5 after September loan-origination volume hit $1.378B (daily avg $53.1M, up from $50.7M in August) and the Upstart Macro Index improved slightly to 1.49; still near 52-week lows after a rough month (-9.7%) on rate-sensitivity. Origination reacceleration reinforces the incoming-CEO insider-buy thesis; no new negative catalysts. Return -5.9% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.6%.

HOLD: two plaintiff-firm 'investigations' launched (Berger Montague 9/14, Bernstein Liebhard) into the board alleging AVAV concealed competitive exposure on the Space Force SCAR program -- no filed suit yet; BofA cut PT to $185 from $225 and Goldman to $285 from $326 (both keep Buy) while UBS raised to $170 (Neutral). These are standard solicitation announcements, not a filed complaint, and PT cuts still imply Buy ratings; underlying backlog/contract-win story (record $1.5B backlog, Titan/LOCUST wins) is intact. Watch for an actual complaint next cycle. Return -1.0% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.5%.

HOLD, flagged for monitoring: new negative -- B. Riley downgraded to Neutral/$65 PT citing launch delays/competition, and a securities fraud class action was filed alleging AST misled investors on capital needs/competition (lead plaintiff deadline 11/13/26); stock down ~6.5% for the week to $57.28. Offsetting positives: 3 more BlueBird satellites shipped to Cape Canaveral (10/1), Telus completed its first network integration test, new Chief Commercial Officer hired (10/2). Litigation is at filing stage only -- not yet thesis-breaking; watch for an amended complaint or certification news next cycle. Return -1.4% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.9%.

HOLD: fundamentals/price confirmed clean today (revenue growth +28%, earnings growth +44.2%, forward P/E 17.2, trading normally at $182.91) -- no disruption evident in the data. One research pass flagged a reported Reverse Morris Trust combination of a 'Performance Technologies' business with Gentherm (10/1) and an Oppenheimer PT cut to $260 from $300 (10/2, Buy maintained); this is unconfirmed against the clean fetched fundamentals/price action and is being treated as a watch item pending corroboration next cycle, not acted on today. Data-center liquid-cooling demand thesis unchanged. Return -1.1% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.6%.

HOLD: new $56M order in the Precision Strike business (electronic safe & arm devices for a European loitering-munition program), layered on 5 additional defense-tech acquisitions this month, continuing the roll-up strategy. Adds to backlog but reinforces the existing M&A-driven-revenue quality flag (~92% of the recent revenue surge is acquisition-driven) rather than resolving it. Return +0.4% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.8%.

HOLD (bullish lean): largest-ever commercial Electron deal -- a 20-launch agreement with Japan's Synspective (2028-31) pushing total launch backlog above 100 missions, shares +7% on the news (~10/1-2). Also Citi initiated Buy/$105 PT, a record $266M Space Force contract, and Iridium shareholders approved the pending acquisition. No negative catalysts found. Return +4.5% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.3%.

HOLD: Jefferies maintained Buy but cut its PT to $68 from $80 (10/1) -- a modest valuation reset after a big run, not a fundamental deterioration; offsetting positives include $100M+ in new space/cyber contracts (10/5) and continued progress on the GEK800/F143 turbofan ignition milestone with GE (confirmed 9/21), with talk of a dedicated solid rocket motor campus. Q2 revenue +30.5% YoY to $458.8M, beat by ~12%. Return -10.5% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.4%.

HOLD: appointed Robert Hunter as UnitedHealthcare president (9/28); announced a 2027 Medicare Advantage strategy with narrower networks aimed at cost containment (10/1). Stock still ~20% below its 52-week high with elevated pre-earnings caution over commercial medical-cost-ratio trends; Q3 report due 10/13 is the next real test. No new negative catalyst beyond the known, already-reflected medical-cost-ratio overhang. Return +2.0% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.7%.

HOLD: successful first Merlin satellite launch (10/2) plus three more satellites (2x NewSat Mark VI, 1x Mark V) slated for October; confirmed expanded Slingshot III deal with ONR/Innovative Defense Technologies (consistent with the 9/14 item already tracked). 5 analysts hold a median PT of $10 (~85% implied upside). Incrementally positive -- launch cadence plus defense-contract expansion -- no negative news found. Return -13.8% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.3%.

HOLD: Wells Fargo trimmed its PT to $380 from $390 (Overweight maintained, routine valuation reset); won a $113M Navy helicopter-engine support contract; declared a $0.47/share dividend (payable 10/26). Consensus remains Buy (21 analysts, avg PT ~$397). Q3 earnings due 10/20 (Street models adj. EPS $2.01, +21% YoY) is the next real catalyst to watch; backlog/guidance story unchanged. Return -1.9% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.5%.
